texts.preamble: Fi vs . Suresh Bansal Page 1 Of 13 on 20 March, 2013 In The Court Of Shri Balwant Rai Bansal Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrateii, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi C.C. No. 209/03 Food Inspector Department of Pfa Govt. of Nct of Delhi A20, Lawrence Road, Delhi 35 ........ Complainant Versus Sh. Suresh Bansal S/o late Sh. Sunder Lal Bansal M/s Bansal Corner, C3/1, Yamuna Vihar, Delhi - 53 R/o C3/1, Yamuna Vihar, Delhi 53
texts.facts: The present complaint has been filed on 24.04.2003 by the Delhi Administration through FI Sh. Suniti Kumar Gupta against the accused Sh. Suresh Bansal. It is stated in the complaint that on 10.07.2002 at about 4.30 PM, FI Sh. Suniti Kumar Gupta purchased a sample of Rai Whole, a food article for analysis from Sh. Suresh Bansal S/o late Sh. Sunder Lal Bansal at M/s Bansal Corner, C 3/1, Yamuna Vihar, Delhi53, who was found conducting the business of the said food article at the Fi vs . Suresh Bansal Page 1 Of 13 on 20 March, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88656254/ 1 time of sampling. FI Sh. Suniti Kumar Gupta purchased approximately 600 gms. of Rai Whole, taken from a jar closed with lid. The sample was taken after mixing the Rai Whole with the help of a clean and dry Jhaba. Thereafter, the sample was divided into three equal parts by putting it in three clean and dry bottles and each bottle containing the sample was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to the PFA Act and Rules. The signatures of vendor were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the bottles containing the sample. Notice was given to accused and price of sample was also paid to the accused vide vendor receipt dated 10.07.2002. Panchnama was also prepared at the spot. All these documents prepared by FI Sh. Suniti Kumar Gupta were signed by accused Sh. Suresh Bansal, the vendor and the other witness namely Ms. Usha Kiran, FI. It is stated that before starting sample proceedings, efforts were made to get the public witnesses to join the proceedings, but none came forward and as such Ms. Usha Kiran, FI joined as witness. It is also stated that the sample was taken under the supervision of Sh. P.C. Jain, SDM/LHA. 2. It is further stated that one counterpart of the sample in intact condition was sent to the Public Analyst, Delhi and two counterparts of the sample in intact conditions were deposited with LHA. The Public Analyst analysed the sample and opined that "the sample is adulterated because it contains unpermitted oil soluble colouring matter". It is further stated that Sh. Suresh Bansal was the VendorcumProprietor of M/s Bansal Corner and he being the incharge of the shop and was responsible for the day to day conduct of the business of the said shop. Thereafter, the entire case file was sent to the Director, PFA who accorded the requisite consent U/s 20 of the Act and consequent thereto the present complaint was filed for violation of provisions of section 2 ((ia) (h), (j) & (m) of the PFA Act, 1954 which is punishable U/s 16 (1) (A) r/w Section 7 of the said Act. 3. The accused was summoned vide order dated 24.04.2003. The accused appeared and moved an application U/s 13 (2) of the Act to get analyzed the second counterpart of the sample from Central Food Laboratory (CFL). The said application was allowed and consequently second counterpart of the sample was sent to CFL, Pune for analysis. Director, CFL on analysing the second counterpart of the sample in question opined vide his Certificate dated 18.06.2003 that "sample does not conform to the standards of Mustard (Rai, Sarson) as per PFA Rules 1955" 4. Charge for voilation of Section 2 (ia) (a) (b), (j) & (m) of the PFA Act and for violation of Rule 23 r/w Rule 28 & 29 of PFA Rules punishable U/s 16 (1A) r/w Section 7 of the said was framed against the accused vide order dated 14.09.2009 to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 5. Thereafter, prosecution examined 4 witnesses namely FI Baljit Singh as PW1, FI Sh. Suniti Kumar Gupta as PW2, Sh. P.C. Jain as PW3 and FI Ms. Usha Kiran as PW4 and PE was closed vide order dated 07.07.2010. 6. Statement of accused U/s 313 Cr.P.C. was recorded on 05.10.2010 wherein accused claimed himself to be innocent and opted for to lead evidence in his defence. 7. The accused has examined Sh. S.N. Mahendru as DW1 in his defence and DE was closed vide order dated 10.05.2011. Fi vs . Suresh Bansal Page 1 Of 13 on 20 March, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88656254/ 2 8. 9. Ld. Counsel for accused has argued that there is variations in the report of Public Analyst (PA) and Central Food Laboratory (CFL) and it shows that sample was not properly mixed and homogenized.
texts.arguments: He further argued that Public Analyst did not find any synthetic colour in the sample and the sample is found to be coloured with unpermitted oil soluble added colouring matter as per PA report, while Director, CLF found two synthetic colour in the sample and it shows that wrong method of detecting the colour in the sample was adopted. He has further argued that unless the colour is identified, there is possibility that colours detected in the sample are the inherent colours of the sample of Rai Whole. 10. On the other hand, the Ld. SPP for complainant has argued that variation in the report of PA and Director, CFL is of no consequence. He contended that as per report of Director, CFL, the sample does not conform to the standards of Mustard (Rai, Sarson) and the report of Director, CFL being conclusive and supersedes the report of Public Analyst, therefore the accused cannot be given benefit of variations in the reports of PA and CFL. 11. All the witnesses examined by the prosecution have deposed more or less as per the averments made in the complaint. PW1 FI Baljeet Singh has deposed in his examinationinchief that on 10.07.2002 he along with FI Ms. Usha Kiran under the supervisions and directions of SDM/LHA Sh. P.C. Jain visited the premises of M/s Bansal Corner, C3/1, Yamuna Vihar, Delhi where accused was found conducting the business of food articles stored there for sale for human consumption including Rai Whole. He has further deposed that he purchased 600 gms of Rai Whole from the accused taken from a jar closed with lid bearing no label declaration for analysis on payment of Rs. 13.20/ vide vendor's receipt Ex. PW1/A. He further deposed that before taking the sample, the Rai Whole was properly homogenized with the help of clean and dry Jhaba by rotating it in all possible directions and thereafter he divided the purchased sample into three equal parts by putting them in three clean and dry glass bottles and all the three sample bottles were separately packed, marked, fastened and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules. 12. PW1 has further deposed that he prepared notice PW1/B and panchnama Ex. PW1/C and copy of the notice was also received by the accused and all the above documents were read over and explained to the accused in Hindi and he signed the same. He has also deposed that one counter part of the sample alongwith one copy of memo in Form VII in intact & sealed condition was sent to the PA on 11.07.2002 vide receipt Ex. PW1/D and remaining two counter parts of the sample in a sealed packet were deposited in intact condition with the LHA on 11.07.2002 vide receipt Ex. PW 1/E. He has further deposed that PA report was received which is Ex. PW1/F according to which the sample does not conform to the standards. He has also deposed that thereafter he was dismissed from the service and further action was taken by FI Suniti Kumar Gupta. 13. PW2 Sh. Suniti Kumar Gupta further investigated the matter and sent a letter Ex. PW2/A to the vendor and vide its reply Ex. PW2/B, it was found that accused Sh. Suresh Bansal is the sole proprietor of the said firm. He has also proved the letter sent to STO Ward No. 75 as Ex. PW2/C from the reply of which it was found that no such firm is found registered with the Sales Tax and the Fi vs .
